cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: A new prediction request without data_structure still entered the legacy prediction dispatch and created prediction_results.
impact: Unknown structure can still receive a random split and produce an apparently valid prediction artifact, violating the fail-closed correctness boundary.
lesson: A contract test must exercise the real new-run dispatch seam, not only the typed entrypoint, because an unchanged legacy fallback can bypass the contract entirely.

cause: The typed prediction entrypoint still executed a temporal split and returned a prediction packet instead of refusing the unsupported M0 profile.
impact: The generic path could imply temporal ML support without gap, embargo, and overlap-label controls.
lesson: A temporal split implementation must remain unreachable until its registered safety profile is complete.

cause: The OOS protocol ignored declared frequency_weight and did not reject unsupported sampling_weight or analysis_weight semantics before fitting.
impact: Weight declarations could be silently ignored or fail to reach the estimator, making the three weight meanings non-auditable.
lesson: Weight semantics need an executable positive path and explicit pre-fit rejection tests for every unsupported semantic.

cause: A historical prediction_result without payload_contract was treated as an incomplete v1.8.6 packet and raised instead of being exposed as legacy-only evidence.
impact: Existing prediction runs cannot be read truthfully by the shared consumer projection, and the UI cannot distinguish legacy results from validated v1.8.6 results.
lesson: Legacy compatibility must be decided from the persisted artifact contract boundary and must not fabricate a SplitPlan.

cause: The evidence card only recognized validated and unavailable states, so a readable legacy projection was rendered as contract failure.

evidence.ref: frontend/src/runResult/PredictionResearchEvidenceCard.test.tsx::labels a readable historical result as legacy and not comparable

impact: Users cannot distinguish a readable historical prediction result from an unreadable or invalid v1.8.6 evidence packet.
lesson: Compatibility states need a dedicated user-visible projection with the exact comparability warning.

cause: The durable compare service only admitted ARMA-GARCH pack IDs and had no typed predictive-research or legacy compatibility builder.
impact: Predictive-research runs cannot be compared from persisted evidence, and legacy versus typed results do not receive the required refusal code.
lesson: Compare compatibility must be derived from the shared persisted evidence projection before pack-specific builders are selected.

cause: DiagnosticsStage called run_prediction_model_v186 without binding the function from the orchestrator module.
impact: A declared typed prediction request crashes with NameError before the contract boundary and prevents the MICE fail-closed test from reaching its intended assertion.
lesson: When stages preserve orchestrator monkeypatch seams, every newly dispatched callable needs an explicit local binding and a real workflow test.

cause: The typed prediction entrypoint persisted packets but exposed no graph recorder seam for the required user-visible prediction chain.
impact: Graph consumers cannot see Dataset Snapshot, Split Plan, baseline/candidate models, evaluation, controls, and result as one evidence chain.
lesson: A persistence-only implementation is incomplete when the same evidence must be projected into lineage; test the recorder seam at the entrypoint.

cause: The Report view had no deterministic predictive-research sections consuming the typed evidence projection.
impact: Report users cannot see development, final holdout, negative-control, and limitations evidence from the same validated packets.
lesson: Report integration needs an independently testable projection component before wiring it into the existing AI report flow.

cause: The shared typed consumer projection exposed final OOS, baseline, controls, and limits but omitted persisted development CV evidence.
impact: Report cannot show the development section from the same validated evidence source without re-reading raw packets.
lesson: A consumer projection must carry every bounded report section required by the contract; consumers must not parse packets independently.

cause: The stored comparison drawer rendered only generic ARMA-GARCH packet fields and ignored the predictive-research compare schema.

evidence.ref: frontend/src/lineage/detail/sections/CompareNodeSection.test.tsx::renders typed predictive-research comparability from the durable packet

impact: Users can create a predictive comparison but cannot see its SplitPlan comparability, metric differences, or legacy-only warning in the graph drawer.
lesson: A durable backend packet is not a user-visible capability until its dedicated consumer renders the packet contract.

cause: The frozen Context Pack already includes the continuation file's listed HTTP, frontend API, draft, table, and API-test paths, but the current predictive compare implementation also modifies frontend/src/lineage/detail/sections files that are outside the frozen allowlist.
impact: The compare UI change cannot be formally verified against the frozen scope until the exact detail-section paths are added through the audited rescope flow.
lesson: Audit the frozen allowlist against every changed consumer path before continuing integration work.

cause: Affected paths differ from the frozen Context Pack and require an explicit scope correction.
lesson: Record the exact old and new manifest identities before correcting development scope.

cause: An explicit Context Pack rescope replaced the affected-path snapshot.
lesson: Correct scope only through an audited, new frozen manifest generation.

cause: The v1.8.6 dispatch correctly stopped using the legacy prediction runner, but two existing workflow tests still patched that retired default seam and therefore lost their structured failure evidence; the new typed runner was also temporarily re-exported in the orchestrator namespace.
impact: The full backend gate reported three code-level failures before the dispatch seam and tests were aligned with the v1.8.6 contract.
lesson: When a correctness contract removes a default path, migrate old failure-injection tests to the explicit typed seam and keep namespace compatibility deliberate.

cause: Negative-control packets initially contained only seeded receipts and no comparable model metrics or fold-level noise importance evidence.
impact: A run could claim to have run controls while giving consumers no evidence that permutation performance degraded or noise was unstable across folds.
lesson: Persist bounded control metrics, development-CV distributions, metric gaps, and model-agnostic fold permutation importance rather than receipt-only status.

cause: The independent v1.8.6 statistical operators produced typed individual results, but no versioned workbench.statistics.evidence-packet producer existed.
impact: Table, Report, and Agent could not receive an independent schema-validated statistics evidence packet without reinterpreting raw test outputs.
lesson: Keep independent statistical evidence in a versioned packet and explicitly preserve its non-model-selection boundary.

cause: The low-level OOS protocol still accepted a temporal SplitPlan after the public entrypoint had been guarded, leaving a direct execution seam outside the M0 fail-closed boundary.
impact: A direct protocol caller could execute temporal ML despite the M0 release boundary.
lesson: Repeat fail-closed profile checks at the protocol boundary and validate declared required columns before refusal.

cause: The agent-seatbelt full fallback reported sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted in code-execution tests; baseline attribution must still be performed on a supported host before this is classified as inherited.
impact: The in-sandbox full gate cannot yet be used as release evidence for code-execution containment behavior.
lesson: Separate product regression evidence from host containment capability and compare the same gate on a supported host and exact baseline.

cause: The full quick gate reached an existing HTTP prediction test that creates a new run without declaring prediction_data_structure; v1.8.6 correctly blocked the run as unknown instead of writing the legacy artifact.
impact: The test suite still encoded the removed legacy default and could not serve current v1.8.6 gate evidence until migrated.
lesson: When a new-run boundary removes a default path, migrate every real HTTP fixture that intentionally expects the old artifact, including tests outside the initial focused list.

lesson: Correct scope only through an audited, new frozen manifest generation.

cause: The HTTP fixture now declares iid explicitly, so it exercises the v1.8.6 typed prediction path and persists the artifact it is intended to fetch.
impact: The quick-gate regression caused by the stale new-run fixture is resolved without restoring the legacy fallback.
lesson: Every real new-run fixture that expects typed prediction evidence must declare its data structure.

cause: The exact baseline 7e257f2 and current v1.8.6 full gates both passed after the baseline worktree received the repository-prescribed shared dependencies.
impact: Baseline attribution is complete; current quick and full gates, golden 23, frontend tests, and typecheck provide release-boundary evidence.
lesson: Baseline gate comparisons must satisfy the same dependency preflight before their results are compared.

cause: The current quick and full gates passed on the supported host without sandbox-exec containment errors, after the earlier agent-seatbelt failure was isolated as a host capability symptom.
impact: The containment gate has supported-host evidence; no skip or xfail was added to hide the earlier failure.
lesson: Host containment failures must be rerun on a supported host before being classified as product regressions or inherited defects.

cause: The completed v1.8.6 integration changes include eight paths that are not present in the currently frozen Context Pack allowlist, so the formal line scope does not faithfully describe the already committed work.

impact.required_action: Use devline_control.py rescope-context to record the affected paths and add each path to the explicit allowlist before continuing implementation.

lesson: A completed commit does not prove formal scope correctness; audit the frozen allowlist against the complete diff before starting an expansion.
